questions.question: By which amendment of the Constitution of India were the terms ‘socialist’ and ‘secular’ added in the preamble?
questions.solution:
The terms ‘socialist’ and ‘secular’ (along with ‘integrity’) were added to the Preamble by the Constitution (Forty-Second Amendment) Act, 1976. This amendment is famously known as the 'Mini-Constitution' because of the vast number of changes it brought to the Indian Constitution during the Emergency.

Note: The Preamble has been amended only once in the history of India.

questions.question: ______ holds office from the date of his/her election till immediately before the first meeting of the Lok Sabha after the dissolution of the one to which he/she was elected.
questions.solution:
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha holds office from the date of his/her election until immediately before the first meeting of the new Lok Sabha after dissolution. This ensures that the office of the Speaker is never vacant during the transition between two Parliaments.

Note: On the first meeting of the new House, a Speaker Pro Tem is usually appointed to administer oaths before a new Speaker is elected.

questions.question: The normal term of every Lok Sabha is ______ years.
questions.solution:
The normal term of every Lok Sabha is 5 years from the date of its first meeting. However, it can be dissolved earlier by the President. During a National Emergency, this term can be extended by Parliament by law for one year at a time.

Key Fact: The Rajya Sabha, unlike the Lok Sabha, is a permanent body and never undergoes dissolution.

questions.question: According to Article 24 of the Constitution of India, a person below ______ years of age shall not be employed to work in any factory.
questions.solution:
According to Article 24 of the Constitution of India, no child below the age of 14 years shall be employed to work in any factory or mine or engaged in any other hazardous employment. This is a Fundamental Right aimed at protecting children from exploitation.

Related: Article 23 prohibits human trafficking and forced labor (begar).

questions.question: Who among the following is NOT a part of the committee, which is constructed to provide suggestions to the Prime Minister regarding the appointment of a chief commissioner of Central Information Commission?
questions.option_3: A Union Cabinet Minister appointed by Prime Minister
questions.option_4: Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha
questions.solution: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is NOT a part of the selection committee for the Chief Information Commissioner. According to the Right to Information Act, the committee consists of: (1) The Prime Minister (Chairperson), (2) The Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, and (3) A Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister.

questions.question: Which of the following was the first High Court established in India?
questions.solution:
The Calcutta High Court was the first High Court established in India. It was established on 1 July 1862 under the High Courts Act, 1861. It was followed shortly after by the Madras and Bombay High Courts in the same year.

Note: The Calcutta High Court has jurisdiction over West Bengal and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

questions.question: Which was the first part of India to hold an election based on universal adult franchise?
questions.solution:
Manipur was the first part of India to hold an election based on universal adult franchise. This historic election took place in June 1948, before India’s first general elections in 1951-52.

Context: The election was held to constitute the Manipur State Legislative Assembly under the Manipur State Constitution Act, 1947.

questions.question: Which of the following provisions and the constitutions of different countries from which they have been adopted in the Constitution of India has been INCORRECTLY paired?
questions.option_1: Principals of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity - Canadian Constitution
questions.option_2: The idea of the rule of law - British Constitution
questions.option_3: Charter of Fundamental rights - United States Constitution
questions.option_4: Directive Principles of State Policy - Irish Constitution
questions.solution:
The pair 'Principles of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity - Canadian Constitution' is INCORRECTLY paired. These principles were actually adopted from the French Constitution (inspired by the French Revolution).

Correct Sources: Rule of Law is from Britain, Fundamental Rights are from the USA, and DPSP is from the Irish Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India details 'Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth'?
questions.solution:
Article 15 of the Indian Constitution prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth. It ensures that no citizen is denied access to shops, public restaurants, hotels, or the use of wells and tanks based on these grounds.

Note: Article 15(3) allows the state to make special provisions for women and children.

questions.question: Who was the President of the Indian National Congress when India won its freedom in the year 1947?
questions.solution:
Acharya J.B. Kripalani was the President of the Indian National Congress in 1947 when India achieved independence. He presided over the Meerut session in 1946.

Additional Info: He was a noted Gandhian, socialist, and a prominent figure in the Indian independence movement.

questions.question: What is the minimum age requirement for appointment as a Governor?
questions.solution:
The minimum age requirement for appointment as a Governor of a state is 35 years. This is specified under Article 157 of the Constitution.

Other Qualifications: The person must be a citizen of India and should not hold any office of profit or be a member of either House of Parliament or State Legislature.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India mentions 'Continuance of the rights of citizenship'?
questions.solution:
Article 10 of the Constitution of India deals with the 'Continuance of the rights of citizenship'. It states that every person who is or is deemed to be a citizen of India shall continue to be such citizen, subject to the provisions of any law made by Parliament.

Note: Article 11 empowers Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law.

questions.question: The total number of fundamental duties provided by the Constitution of India is:
questions.solution: The total number of Fundamental Duties provided by the Constitution is 11. Originally, there were no fundamental duties; 10 were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976). The 11th duty (providing education opportunities to children) was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India makes provision for protection in respect of conviction for offences?
questions.solution: Article 20 provides protection in respect of conviction for offences. It includes three protections: (1) No ex-post-facto law (cannot be punished for an act that wasn't a crime when committed), (2) No double jeopardy (cannot be punished twice for the same offence), and (3) No self-incrimination (cannot be forced to be a witness against oneself).

questions.question: Which of the following does the Special Marriage Act 1954 NOT support?
questions.solution:
The Special Marriage Act 1954 was designed to facilitate civil marriages regardless of the faith or caste of the parties. Therefore, it does NOT support strict endogamy (the practice of marrying only within one's own social group/caste).

Purpose: It supports inter-faith and inter-caste marriages to promote communal harmony and secularism.

questions.question: Which of the following writs is a challenge to the legality of a prisoner's detention?
questions.solution:
The writ of Habeas Corpus is a challenge to the legality of a prisoner's detention. Literally meaning 'to have the body', it is an order issued by the court to a person who has detained another, to produce the body of the latter before it so the court can examine the lawfulness of the detention.

Note: It can be issued against both public authorities and private individuals.

questions.question: In which year did Nepal adopt its first democratic constitution?
questions.solution:
Nepal adopted its first democratic constitution on 20 September 2015. This marked Nepal's transition from a Hindu monarchy to a secular, federal democratic republic.

Background: The constitution was the result of years of political transition following the end of the decade-long Maoist insurgency and the abolition of the monarchy in 2008.

questions.question: Which amendment of the Constitution of India incorporated Goa, Daman and Diu as the eighth union territory of India, by amending the First Schedule to the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The 12th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1962 incorporated Goa, Daman and Diu as a Union Territory of India. These territories were liberated from Portuguese rule in December 1961 following 'Operation Vijay'.

Note: Goa later became a full-fledged state in 1987 via the 56th Amendment.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India envisages that a person shall NOT be qualified to be chosen to fill up a seat in the Parliament unless he is a citizen of India?
questions.solution:
Article 84 sets the qualifications for membership of Parliament. It states that a person must be a citizen of India, make an oath/affirmation, and meet the age requirement (25 for Lok Sabha, 30 for Rajya Sabha).

Note: Article 61 deals with the impeachment of the President, and Article 52 states there shall be a President.

questions.question: A ______ helps serve as a set of rules and principles that all persons in a country can agree upon as the basis of the way in which they want the country to be governed.
questions.solution:
A Constitution serves as a set of rules and principles that all persons in a country can agree upon as the basis of how they want to be governed. it defines the relationship between the citizens and the government, as well as the distribution of power among various organs of the state.

Concept: It is the supreme law of a nation.

questions.question: According to the fundamental rights provided by the Constitution of India, the state is bound to provide free and compulsory education to all children from the age of:
questions.solution:
As per Article 21A (added by the 86th Amendment), the State must provide free and compulsory education to all children from the age of 6 to 14 years. This is a Fundamental Right.

Additional Info: The Right to Education (RTE) Act was enacted in 2009 to give effect to this constitutional provision.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India is related to the oath or affirmation by the President?
questions.solution:
Article 60 of the Indian Constitution is related to the oath or affirmation by the President. The oath is administered by the Chief Justice of India (or the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court in their absence).

Note: Article 54 deals with the election of the President, and Article 57 deals with eligibility for re-election.

questions.question: According to which of the following Schedules to the Constitution provides for allocation of seats to the states and union territories in Rajya Sabha?
questions.solution:
The Fourth Schedule of the Constitution provides for the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha to the States and Union Territories. The allocation is based on the population of each state.

Related: The Seventh Schedule deals with the distribution of powers between the Union and States (Union, State, and Concurrent Lists).

questions.question: How many Rajya Sabha seats come from the state of Assam?
questions.solution:
There are 7 seats allocated to the state of Assam in the Rajya Sabha.

Comparative Stats: In the Lok Sabha, Assam has 14 seats. Uttar Pradesh has the highest representation in the Rajya Sabha with 31 seats, followed by Maharashtra with 19.
